title: Ա Ղ Օ Թ Ա Գ Ի Ր Ք

fields.titre: Ա Ղ Օ Թ Ա Գ Ի Ր Ք
fields.informations_diverses: Date: 16th (possibly 15th century: see note below). Vellum, codex; 22.5x19.5 cm; 167 folios; Full binding, wooden boards covered with very beautifully designed leather covers with detailed geometrical patterns. 2 columns, 17 lines per column. Ms. stained throughout; however, the beautifully and exquisitely executed handwriting is excellent and legible throughout. Overall, this is a bery beautiful Ms.
fields.contenu:
Title: Weddase Amlak or Prayers for the Seven Days of the Week (also entitled in this Ms. as Book of Petitions and Supplications). 1) fols. 4—23. Prayer of Basil for Monday. 2) fols. 24—53a. Prayer of St. Ephrem for Tuesday. 3) fols. 53b—74. Second prayer of ST. Ephrem for Wednesday. 4) fols. 75—103a. Prayer of John the Elder for Thursday. 5) fols. 103b—122. Prayer of Abba Pachomius for Friday. 6) fols. 123—137. Prayer of Athanasius, Pat. of Alexandria for the "Jewish Sabbath". 7) fols. 138—153 . Prayer of Cyril. Pat. of Alexandria for the Christian Sabbath. 8) fols. 154—158a. Prayer of Thanksgiving (Praise Be To Thee) attributed to Phalaskinos of Manbuzar. 9) fols. 158a—164a. Short prayers or petitions for the seven days of the week.
Additional Content. ... If the manuscript was written for Emperor Ba'eda Maryam (1468—78), then we have more or less the exact date for its writing, except for the fact that the handwriting is not of the 15th century type. 2) fols. 1b—3. A direction for computing the different hours of the day during the different months of the year based on the position of the sun at the different times. 3) fols. 115b—116a. A short prayer of Thanksgiving based on God's appearance to Abraham under the Mamre tree. 4) fols. 116b and 117a. Two alternative pen trials. 5) fols. 1a, 164b, 165a, 167b. Blank.
